hints: Notice the resultant must have zero east-west component, so the eastward part of the $800 \text{ km h}^{-1}$ velocity must cancel the $200 \text{ km h}^{-1}$ wind to the west.
Connect the eastward component to angle $\theta$ east of north using $800 \sin\theta$ and set it equal to $200 \text{ km h}^{-1}$.
Find $\theta$ from $\sin\theta = 0.25$, then keep only the north part $800 \cos\theta$ for the resultant magnitude in $\text{km h}^{-1}$.
walkthrough: Resolve the $800 \text{ km h}^{-1}$ aircraft velocity: east component is $800 \sin\theta$ and north component is $800 \cos\theta$, while wind velocity is $200 \text{ km h}^{-1}$ to the west.
For a resultant due north the total east-west velocity must be zero, so $800 \sin\theta - 200 = 0$.
The northward resultant is the north component: $v = 800 \cos\theta \approx 800 \times 0.968 \approx 774 \text{ km h}^{-1}$, about $770 \text{ km h}^{-1}$.
The $770 \text{ km h}^{-1}$ value is sensibly less than $800 \text{ km h}^{-1}$ because only part of the aircraft velocity points north. This is option A.

options.A: East component $800 \sin\theta = 200$ gives $\theta \approx 14^{\circ}$ and north component $800 \cos\theta \approx 770 \text{ km h}^{-1}$.
options.B: Angle is about $14^{\circ}$ but $820 \text{ km h}^{-1}$ is larger than $800 \text{ km h}^{-1}$ and cannot be the north component of an $800 \text{ km h}^{-1}$ vector.
options.C: $76^{\circ}$ uses $\cos\theta = 200/800$ instead of $\sin\theta = 200/800$ for the east-west balance.
options.D: $76^{\circ}$ swaps sine and cosine, and $820 \text{ km h}^{-1}$ incorrectly adds instead of finding the smaller north component.
